description:
Found by the fz-kdt.127 research (2026-09-02, HEAD 172ab21f1; probes
scratchpad probeB1.fz, pin6gb.fz, canon dumps beside them).

A lambda that captures a callable and calls it -- `fn mk(g), do: fn (n) ->
g.(n) end`; make_reducer's `predicate.(entry)` in the fz-6gb pin -- is keyed
once per captured IDENTITY (consumes_callable_identity: capture params /
ClosureCall / Lambda, jobs/keying.rs:257), e.g. mk/1#lambda[fnref[double]]
and [fnref[triple]]. Both bodies compile the call as `closure_call ...
callee=v0 target=-` with v0 carried as `callable(<unknown>/0) carrier=
ValueRef tys=[any]`: the captured fn is NOT grounded (escape raised by
boundary_value_demand, runtime_demand.rs:3029-3036), the call goes through
the captured value's own code word, and the two specializations differ in
nothing. This is why the same-layout/different-identity population
(probeB1 4/9, probeB2 6/-6, 00281, the six fz-kdt.125 residue groups) is
correct today although their forwarder-hosted dispatch has no question:
arm 0 takes all and it does not matter.

Two consequences to settle:
 (1) proportional compilation: one body per captured identity buys
     nothing here -- the per-identity split should collapse where the
     body does not ground the capture, or the capture should ground to a
     direct call (the key pins one target; kdt.152's exact layout would
     be Absent) -- pick by measurement (closure_allocs pins, wall clock).
 (2) the fz-6gb pin drive_test.rs:4869 compiler2_native_program_keeps_
     distinct_direct_callable_executables_for_same_surface_when_capture_
     identity_differs asserts two such duplicates exist and its "direct"
     rationale is not what the artifact does; rewrite the pin to what it
     actually protects (or delete it with the collapse).
Sequence after fz-kdt.127 (whose shape axis gives these arms a real
question, so the collapse must be measured against live arms).
title: Identity-specialized lambda bodies that call their captured callable through its word are byte-duplicates
